requirement:
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its fenced declaration, including its complete body but excluding anchor option lines, MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
The subject `requirements.authoring_input` has three obligations: the subject's fenced declaration is in the mandatory input set, it includes the complete body, and it excludes anchor option lines. The reviewed tests cover all three.

- **Declaration is included.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment]` asserts that the mandatory input set for `requirements.ready` is exactly one entry. That entry has `requirements`, `matches` and `text` equal to `[":::{req} ready", "The project MUST be ready.", ":::"]`. That is the full fence, including the opening and closing lines.
- **Declaration is included for other subject kinds.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` checks the same inclusion for an example subject (`requirements.case`). The first input is that example, with its complete fenced text. For `requirements.ready` it also checks that the input set contains the declaration alongside the other contributions.
- **Complete body.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` uses a multi-line body with a blank line ("The project MUST be ready.", "", "Keep the whole body."). It asserts the whole body appears verbatim in the input `text` and in `subject_text`.
- **Anchor option lines excluded, body lines kept.** The same test declares `:impl:` and `:test:` anchor lines right after the opening fence. It asserts they are absent from the declaration's `text`. It also puts a body line `:impl: this is body text` inside the body and asserts that line is retained. This checks that the exclusion applies only to anchor option lines and not to body text that looks like one.
- **Other tests.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` is marked as a test of the subject. It shows the declaration is still read when files are untracked in git.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these assertions would accept. The assertions use exact equality on the declaration entry, so truncating the body, dropping the fence lines, or leaving anchor lines in would all fail them. The tests also carry `{test}` markers for the subject, so there is no marking gap.
